title: How to test Zuri (2 min)
lines: Welcome, tester. Thank you for helping. This short video shows how we test Zuri, and what we need from you.

Look at the bar at the top. Green with PRACTICE means a pretend company: the customers, payments and jobs are made up, nothing you do reaches the real Zuri or any real customer, and it is saved only on this phone. So try anything — you cannot break it. Orange with TRAINING means the shared training copy: the customers and money are still pretend, but your teammates see what you do. Work there like it is a real day.
Your Testers' List is one page, one step at a time: the videos, the things to try for your job, joining the training copy. Do a step, tap Done, and the next one appears.
Under every step is a box: Tell Claude. Something wrong, confusing, or slow? Write it there. Short is fine: the button is too small, or I did not understand this word.
If you opened Zuri inside Feedback Studio, even better: press the red button and talk while you work. Point at what is wrong. At the end, tap I'm done, then Send to Claude.
At the bottom is the version line. If you report a problem, say which version you had.
The count at the top of your list shows how far you are. Please finish every step for your job. That is how we know Zuri is ready for real customers.
Before you start: watch What Zuri is, five minutes, then the videos for your own job. Then open the checklist and begin. Thank you!

title: Business Week: your coach (2 min)
lines: This is your coach. During Business Week every step shows here, inside Zuri, so you never leave the app.
It says what to do, where, and how you should end. Read it, then do it in Zuri.
Not sure where? Tap Go there, and Zuri opens the right page.
Finished the step? Tap Step done. Then tap a face: how easy was it? This tells us which parts of Zuri are hard.
Something wrong, confusing or slow? Tap Problem and write what happened. Every real problem we confirm pays you one hundred shillings.
Lost? Tap I am stuck. It shows you the way. Being stuck is useful: it shows us where Zuri must be easier.
All today shows every step of your day. You can do them in any order.
The last step of every day is a real-world problem, like a customer calling about a router. No steps are given: do what you would do at work. If you need help, tap Show me how.
Open Zuri from your Business Week page, inside Feedback Studio. There you can also talk, point and take screenshots. At the end of the day, tap Done at the bottom, then Send to Claude. Thank you!

title: What Zuri is — the whole system in 5 minutes
lines: Welcome to Zuri. In the next few minutes you will see the whole system, so you know how everything fits together. After this, watch the short videos for your own job.
Zuri is one app for the whole Zuri Fiber team: the partners, the office, the call center, and the technicians in the field. It works on any phone, in Chrome, and on the office computer.
Everyone works from the same information. This is Home. It shows the whole company on one page: our customers, who has paid, our service jobs, and our money.

Every morning at half past six, the Zuri manager looks at everything and writes each person's list for the day. It also warns us early when something is going wrong, like customers who have not paid, or cash running low.
Needs attention shows the most important problems first. Tap one, and it takes you straight there.
Customers is everyone we serve: their package, their phone number, where they live, and when their payment runs out. The list comes from our billing website every morning.
And the map: every customer with a pin, by area. Green has paid, red has run out. A technician taps a pin and drives there.
Jobs is the work at customers' houses: faults, new installs, moving a router, and payment calls. Each job goes to a technician, with a day to visit.
When a customer's internet runs out, Zuri opens a payment follow-up job by itself. The call center phones the customer, and writes down what they said.
Let's follow one job from start to finish. A customer called: no internet. The call center made this job, and sent it to Peter.
Peter sees the job on his phone, with the customer's number, and a map to the house.
At the house, he taps what he found, what he did, and whether the customer paid him. Then he taps Job finished. If there is no signal, the phone keeps it, and sends it later.
He adds photos, and the parts he used, so the office knows what happened, and what stock is left.
Tasks is everyone's to-do list. Anyone can give anyone a task, and the Zuri manager adds tasks too. When you finish one, tick it, and the person who asked can see it is done.
Money is for the finance team and the partners only. It shows the cash in the bank and on M-Pesa, the bills still to pay, and what is left after the bills.
Zuri also looks thirty days ahead: money coming in from renewals, and bills going out. If cash will run short, it warns us weeks before, not on the day.

And each morning, the pay run: the bills that are due and the staff whose pay day it is, with the number to pay. Send it in M-Pesa, tap Sent, and it is recorded. A second person then approves every payment: money always needs two people.
Every Friday, the report for the partners writes itself, ready to send on WhatsApp.
Each morning, the manager also writes a short WhatsApp message for every staff member, with their most important jobs for the day.
Each person only sees what their job needs. A technician sees only their own jobs. The call center sees jobs and customers. Only finance and the partners see the money.
That is Zuri. Now watch the short videos for your own job, and try everything in practice. Practice uses pretend customers, so you cannot break anything.

title: Welcome to Zuri
lines: Welcome to Zuri. This is the one app for the whole Zuri Fiber team. Your tabs are at the bottom. You only see the tabs your job needs.
Jobs is the work at customers' houses: faults, new installs, and calls about payment.
Tasks is your to-do list. Anyone can give anyone a task. Every morning the Zuri manager adds what needs doing.
Me has your account, these videos, and anything waiting to send.
No signal? No problem. Zuri saves your work on the phone and sends it when signal comes back. A yellow badge at the top shows how many things are waiting.
Working in bright sun? Choose Light. It is the easiest to read outside.
To put Zuri on your home screen: open it in Chrome, tap the three dots, then Add to Home screen. That's it. Now pick the video for your job.

title: Your task list
lines: This is Tasks. My day shows what is yours. Team shows everyone's list.
Each task says who it is from and when it is due. High and urgent tasks come first.
Finished? Tick the box. The person who gave it to you can see it is done.
Stuck, or need to explain something? Tap Notes and write it. Everyone on the task sees your note.
Type your note and tap Add.
To give someone a task, tap Add a task. Write what needs doing in a few words.
Then choose who should do it: a person, or a whole group like Field techs.
Tap Add task. It appears on their list straight away, even if you have no signal yet.

title: 1 · 6:45 am — Kelvin opens the day
lines: It is a quarter to seven in Maai Mahiu. Kelvin opens Zuri with his tea. The Zuri manager ran at half past six: here is what it noticed overnight.
Needs attention. Two things today: the Zuri B float is below target, and ten customers have run out of paid time.
His own list for the day, already written: a cash count, a bill to pay, statements to sort. He will tick them as he goes.
Money, Cash today. The bank, the M-Pesa float, bills owing, and cash after bills, for each area. The float warning is here too.
First job: a cash count. He opens the bank app and the M-Pesa account on his phone, and types what each one says.
Save. Now the forecast for the next thirty days starts from a true number.
Next, the pay run. Build today's list collects every bill that is due and every monthly salary whose day has come. Anything left unpaid from last month stays on the list.
KPLC is due today, and so is Mary's salary. He copies the number, sends each one in the M-Pesa app, and comes back.
Then Sent, and the code from the M-Pesa message. Zuri records it as an expense, with his name and the time, and it waits for a second person, Jerry, to approve it.
Dickson forwards an M-Pesa message: cable clips from the hardware shop. Kelvin pastes it in and taps Read the message.
The code, the amount, the shop, the date, even the new M-Pesa balance: filled in. He checks the category and saves.
The bank statement came in yesterday; twelve lines still to sort. That is an afternoon job. For now, the phones are starting to ring.

title: 2 · 8:30 am — Mary at the call center
lines: Half past eight. Mary opens Jobs. Overnight, Zuri opened a payment follow-up for every customer whose internet ran out. These are her calls for the morning.
She opens Grace Njeri, the most overdue.
Her package ran out more than a week ago. She taps Call. The customer says: Friday, when the salary comes.
So: Will pay, in three days. The job comes back on Friday to be checked.
The phone rings. John Mwangi, near the market: no internet since morning, the router light is red. Mary starts a new job and finds him.
Fault. She writes what he said, in his words.
Peter covers the market. She sends it to him for today, and saves.
One more tap: Tell Peter on WhatsApp. The message has the customer, the problem and the map. He sees it before he has finished his tea.

title: 3 · 9:15 am — Peter on the road
lines: Quarter past nine. Peter checks his list on the motorbike. The new job from Mary is at the top, marked urgent.
He opens it.
He calls John to say he is ten minutes away, and opens the map.
At the gate: I'm starting now. Back at the office, Mary sees the job turn to In progress.
Twenty minutes later it is fixed. He taps what he found: a bad connector.
And what he did: replaced the connector, tested.
John pays this month's two thousand on the spot, by M-Pesa. Peter taps M-Pesa, the amount, and the code from John's message.
Job finished. The payment goes straight to the books, and Kelvin never has to chase it.
The job leaves his list. Next one. If the signal drops in the valley, the phone keeps everything and sends it later.

title: 4 · 2:00 pm — Kelvin's afternoon
lines: Two o'clock. The phones are quiet. Kelvin sorts the statement lines from yesterday's bank statement. This one is a customer payment.

A KPLC line: he ticks Always first, then picks Rent and Utilities, so every KPLC line sorts itself from now on. Forgot to tick it? After sorting, tap Always sort like this. Twelve lines take five minutes.
Who paid. Late: the customers who have run out. Each one has a Call button and a ready-made WhatsApp reminder.
He sends one reminder to a customer who always pays after a nudge.
The next thirty days. The lowest point is above zero: good. If it were not, he would tell Jerry today, not on the day it bites.
Back to his list. Cash count, done. Pay run, done. Statements, done. Three ticks.

title: 5 · 5:00 pm — the partners close the day
lines: Five o'clock. Jerry, a partner, looks at Home from Chicago. Faults fixed today, installs waiting, the late count down by one, cash still fine.
Team: what is still open across everyone. Nothing stuck more than two days, so nothing has escalated.
Jerry gives Peter a task for tomorrow: check the splitter at the market, two customers say it is slow at night.
On Friday there is one more step: the report writes itself. Copy, paste into the partners' WhatsApp group. Jerry reads it in Chicago over breakfast.
And tomorrow at half past six it starts again: the manager writes everyone's list, and a WhatsApp nudge for each person. That is a day with Zuri.

title: 1 · Today's texts — the after-cutoff path in one list
lines: This is Mary at the call center. Billnasi texts every customer three days before the package runs out, and then switches them off. Our part starts after the cutoff. Today's texts puts everyone due today in one list. Tap it.
One customer at a time, with the message already written. No more opening each job and looking for which step it is on.
Up here: how many she has done, out of everyone due today.
The customer: their area, account, package and price, and how many days ago they were switched off.
Where they are on the path: day one, help them reconnect. Day three, is anything wrong? Day seven, we miss you. Day fourteen, a last check-in. Day thirty, a kind goodbye.
Today's words, written for this step, with their name, the price and how to pay with the Zuri Paybill.
Tap Text. The phone's own messages app opens with the number and the words. She presses send there. It works without data. Zuri never sends anything by itself.
Zuri wrote it on the customer's job, and moved the job to the day of the next step. If they pay, the billing refresh closes it by itself.
Then Next.
On day three and day fourteen the card says: call first. Ask how the service was. If it was not working, open the job and tap Service problem, so a technician goes.
Some customers answer WhatsApp faster. Tap WhatsApp instead: it opens WhatsApp with the same words.
Next.
Can't reach someone today, or the number is wrong? Skip for today. They come back tomorrow.
The whole list for today: sent, skipped, and still to send. Tap any name to jump to them.
Every morning the Zuri manager puts one task on her list: Today's texts and calls. The old list of customers to remind the day before is gone, because Billnasi already reminds them.

title: 2 · The Friday report writes itself
lines: Friday. Before, Mary and Vero gathered numbers on WhatsApp and Kelvin typed the report. Now Zuri writes it from the week's real work. This is Kelvin.
First, a check. The cash count is three days old, and the money part starts from it. So Zuri asks for a fresh count before anything else.
Payments recorded but still waiting for a second person's OK are listed, so nothing slips past the partners.
Service this week: new faults, how many were fixed and how fast, what is still open, installs, and any outage.
Payment follow-ups: how many customers are cut off now, how many renewed this week, and how many texts went out.
The team: what each person did in Zuri this week. Jobs finished, texts sent, tasks ticked, receipts snapped. Good work is seen.
Receipts this week, from the receipts videos: spent, with receipts, and missing.
And on Fridays the Zuri manager writes its own summary from the real numbers: what happened, and three decisions for the partners, each with the why.
All of it becomes one message, ready for WhatsApp: the money for each area first, then service, follow-ups, the team, receipts, payments waiting, and the manager's summary.
Tap Copy for WhatsApp, open the partners' group, and paste. That is the whole Friday job now.
Need it on paper, or as a PDF for the bank? Tap Printable view.
A clean page, without the app's buttons and tabs.
Tap Print, or save as PDF from the print screen.

title: 3 · A fault call — but the package expired
lines: A customer calls: my internet is not working. Mary starts a new job and finds her.
Grace Njeri. Tap her.

Zuri warns straight away: her package expired, nine days ago. This is probably not a fault. The billing website switched her off. A technician's visit costs a boda fare and an hour, and paying fixes it in minutes.
So Mary tells her how to pay, and taps Turn this into a payment follow-up. No technician is sent.
She already had a payment follow-up, so Zuri opened it instead of making a second one. The words for her step are ready to send.
The note says why: she called about no internet, the package had expired, help her pay first.
It can also happen the other way: a fault job made before anyone checked. Here is one Dickson made this morning.
The job itself shows the same warning, at the top, before anyone sends a technician.
One tap. If the customer already has a follow-up, Zuri closes this fault job with a note and opens the follow-up. If not, this job becomes the follow-up. Either way, nobody drives out for nothing.
And the call center carries on from the follow-up. It is a warning, never a wall: if the customer really has a fault, just save the job.

title: 4 · Map pins and nearest-first
lines: This is Peter, a field technician, with several jobs today. Tap Nearest first. Zuri uses where the phone is and puts the closest job at the top.
Each job now shows how far away it is. Urgent jobs still stay on top.
If location is switched off on the phone, nothing breaks: the list stays urgent first, then by day, and Zuri says how to switch location on.
This customer has no map pin yet. Peter phoned for directions. Open the job.
No map pin. Before, Peter had to remember to drop one.
Now, when he arrives and taps I'm starting now…
Zuri offers it by itself: save where you are standing as the customer's pin. It checks how accurate the phone is: twelve metres, good.
Yes, save the pin. One tap.
Now the next technician taps Open map and drives straight there.
Some pins were saved indoors, far from the gate. This customer's pin is a hundred and twenty metres off. Open the job.

Zuri marks it rough. When Peter starts this job, Zuri offers to replace it. If the phone itself is only accurate to more than fifty metres, Zuri says so: step outside, wait a minute and try again. The same guard as always.

title: 5 · Outage spotting
lines: Something is wrong in Zuri B. In the last hour, two customers there called: no internet. This is Jerry, a partner, looking at Jobs.
A third call comes in, also from Zuri B.
Mary writes what the caller says.
Save job.
Three fault calls in one area within two hours. Zuri says: possible outage in Zuri B. It is probably the cabinet, the OLT or the backhaul, not three separate houses.
And it put one urgent task on the technical team's list, instead of three separate visits. Dickson checks the equipment for Zuri B first.
For the partners, Home shows the outage with a short notice to the customers, drafted by Zuri. Nothing goes to customers by itself.
Jerry can change the words. Then Yes, or No.
Yes, use this notice.
Now the office copies it into a WhatsApp broadcast to the Zuri B customers. Fewer calls, calmer customers.
While the outage lasts, a new call from Zuri B shows it right on the job form.
So whoever answers can tell the caller: we know, the technicians are on it. The new job joins the outage by itself.
When the service is back, technical or a partner taps Service is back. The outage closes, and so does its task.
Then each fault job from that area is checked and finished as usual.

title: 6 · Two people for every payment — recording
lines: Zuri's rule: money out always needs two people. Now the database enforces it. This is Kelvin. Yesterday he paid the Bayobab backhaul: it says waiting for a second OK. The bill does not count it as paid yet.
Today KPLC is due. He taps Pay.
The sheet says how it works: after he records it, someone else approves it. Best: ask first, send after the OK, then add the code.
He already sent this one, so he types the M-Pesa code.
Pay and record it.
Approvals, under Bills. These are Kelvin's own payments. There is no Approve button for him: someone else must approve them.
If he made a mistake, he can withdraw it, with a reason.
What if someone tried to approve their own payment some other way? The database itself refuses.
Waiting for his OK: payments other people recorded. Field technicians' receipts are here too. They are expenses, and finance confirms them: finance is the second person.
He checks the amount, the person and the receipt, and taps Approve. A payment with no receipt asks first: approve anyway?
Approved this week shows it, with his name and the time.
In practice you can play the second person: switch to Jerry. In real life, it is Jerry's own phone and his own login. The next chapter does exactly that.

title: 6b · Two people for every payment — approving
lines: This is Jerry, a partner, on his own phone. Home says: payments waiting for your OK.
Kelvin's payments are here, with what they were for, the amount, the code and the time.
The Bayobab backhaul looks right. Approve.
Only now does the Bayobab bill count it as paid.
Something wrong? A wrong number, or not a Zuri cost? Decline it and say why. The request is removed, the bill is not touched, and the log keeps it.
The pay run works the same way: Sent puts the line on waiting, and a second person approves it.
The rule lives in Admin, Settings. On means two people for every payment above this amount. Zero means every payment.
Off is only for while just one person has an account. It shows a red warning. When Kelvin has his own login, it stays On.

title: 7 · Your turn — try every time saver
lines: That is the time savers. Now try them yourself, in practice. Nothing here is real.
The Friday report is under Money, Report.
Approvals are under Money, Bills. To try both people, use the practice switch, or Me, Try another job.
Every chapter is on the Learn page, to watch again any time.

title: 1 · An outage: text the whole area
lines: This is Mary at the call center. Three customers in Zuri B called with no internet. Zuri says: possible outage. Soon every phone in Zuri B will be ringing.
So she tells them all at once, before they call. Tap Text the Zuri B customers.
Who gets it: the Zuri B customers. Zuri picked the area from the outage.
Only Active customers. Someone who is switched off isn't affected by an outage.
She fills in when it should be back, as the technicians told her.
And the same in Kiswahili, the way people say it: saa kumi jioni.
This is exactly what the customers will read, in Kiswahili and in English. Each customer gets their own language. It fits in one SMS.

How many customers and phones, how many prefer each language, and anyone left out: people who said no to these messages, or have no phone number. On the free plan it goes by WhatsApp, so there is nothing to pay.
Mary can't send it on her own. She asks a partner for a yes.
Now it waits for a partner. If it's urgent, she phones Jerry: it's on his Home screen.
Every step is written down: who wrote it, who said yes, who sent it, and when. Zuri never sends anything by itself.

title: 2 · A partner says yes, and it goes out
lines: This is Jerry, a partner. Home says: one alert waiting for your yes.
Waiting for a partner: Mary's outage message for Zuri B. He opens it.
He reads the Kiswahili,
and the English. Once he says yes, nobody can change the words or the people. Not even a partner: the database refuses. To change it, cancel it and write a new one.
It's right. Yes, approve.
Now it can go out. Zuri doesn't send it by itself. On the free plan it goes by WhatsApp.
The customers come in groups, by language, up to two hundred and fifty-six in each: the most one WhatsApp broadcast list can take.
Save contacts puts a whole group into the office phone's contacts in one go. Then in WhatsApp: New broadcast, pick them, and paste the words.
Copy the words for that group, paste them into the broadcast, and send. Customers only get broadcasts if they have saved Zuri's number, so ask them to.
To reach every phone, even without WhatsApp, there is Bulk SMS. It's an add-on: you pay only for the texts you send, and only after a partner switches it on.
When it has gone out, tap It went out.
Written by Mary, approved by Jerry, sent, each with the time. That's the whole story of every message the customers got.

title: 3 · Service is back: the same people hear it
lines: Two hours later the technicians fixed the cabinet. This outage message went to the Zuri B customers this morning.
Now those same customers should hear that it's back.
Send FIX to the same people.
Exactly the people who got the outage message. Nobody missed, and nobody who wasn't affected.
Internet is back, thank you for your patience, and what to do if theirs is still off: restart the router, then call or WhatsApp us.
Jerry is a partner, so he can save and approve in one step.
Then the same as before: download the list, send it, and tap It went out.

title: 4 · By cabinet: only the homes on that cabinet
lines: This is Dickson, technical. On Saturday he will work on cabinet A-1. Only the homes wired to that cabinet need to know.
By cabinet or tower.
Every cabinet, tower and OLT on the map. Choosing the OLT reaches everyone behind it.
Cabinet A-1.
Each home goes with the cabinet set on the customer's page, or, if nobody set it, the nearest cabinet on the map.
A home with no map pin and no cabinet can't be placed. Zuri names them, so someone can fix them before Saturday. Or send by area instead.
Planned work needs the day, the time and how long, in English and in Kiswahili.
Planned work in Cabinet A-1, on Saturday from ten, for about two hours. Sent the day before, it saves a morning of calls.
Ask a partner for a yes.
It also starts from the map. Tap a cabinet or tower, then Text the homes on this cabinet.
And from Customers, Alerts. The usual ones are one tap away: outage, service back, planned work, and power cut. Power cut tells customers it's KPLC, not us.

title: 5 · One customer: cabinet, language, and yes to offers
lines: Every customer's page has a new box: Messages.
Which cabinet or tower the home is wired to. Field technicians set it on the job page at the install. Until then, Zuri uses the nearest one.
The language they want. Most get Kiswahili; some prefer English.
Outages and planned work: on for everyone, unless they ask us to stop.
Offers and upgrades: only when the customer says yes. Ask them on the phone.
Then write down how and when they said yes. Zuri won't save a yes to offers without it.
Save.

title: 6 · Partners: the words, the add-ons and quiet hours
lines: The partners own the words. Messages lists every ready-made alert.
Read every Kiswahili message and change anything that doesn't sound right. Keep them short: up to 160 letters is one SMS.
Package ending is off. Billnasi already texts customers three days before the cutoff, so we don't send it twice.
Offers go only to customers who said yes, and never during quiet hours.
Need another one? Add a new message with its own short code.
Plan and add-ons. Alerts works for free, with WhatsApp. Anything that costs money is a switch, and it stays off until Zuri needs it.
When Zuri grows, switch on Bulk SMS. There is no monthly fee: you pay the SMS company only for the texts you send.
The price of one SMS, from the bulk-SMS bill. Then every alert shows its cost before anyone says yes.
The sender name registered with the SMS company, so customers see it's really Zuri.
Later, with the Daraja server, Zuri can send the texts itself, paid from M-Pesa credit with a monthly cap, so there is never a surprise bill.
Quiet hours: offers never go out after seven in the evening. Kenyan rules allow promotional texts only from seven to seven. Outage messages can go any time.
Save.

title: 7 · Email: free, to customers who said yes
lines: Email is free too. Zuri has no email system of its own, so it uses the office email account: Gmail or Outlook.
Only customers who have an email on their page and said yes to emails get one. Everyone else still gets WhatsApp.
Copy the addresses for one batch. In the office email, paste them into BCC. Never To or Cc, or every customer sees everyone else's address.
Then copy the subject and the words. The words end with one line telling the customer how to stop: reply STOP.
On a phone, Open email can fill in all three for you.
If a customer replies STOP, untick Emails on their page. That is all it takes.
On the customer page, in Messages: Emails too. Tick it only when the customer says yes.
And write how and when they said yes. Zuri won't save a yes to emails without it.
Save.

title: 8 · Your turn: try every part of Alerts
lines: That's Alerts. Now try it yourself, in practice. Nothing here is real, and nothing is sent.
Alerts waiting for a partner's yes are here, and on the partners' Home screen.
Everything that went out stays here: who wrote it, who said yes, and when.
Every chapter is on the Learn page, to watch again any time.

title: 1 · Payback and break-even — what they mean
lines: This is Jerry, a partner. Zuri can plan a new area before a shilling is spent, and then watch it against the plan. Home shows one line per project. Tap it.
Projects. Every project goes three steps: plan it, decide together, then track what really happens.
Narok is still a plan. Open it.
The answer comes first, in plain words: how much it costs to start, and the month you get it back.
Two different months matter. Break-even is the first month when the money coming in is more than the money going out that month.
Payback comes later. By then, all the profits added together have paid back the start-up money, and the losses of the early months.
And the most money tied up: the deepest the cash goes. That is how much the partners must have ready, or borrow.
The chart shows it. The line starts below zero: the start-up money going out. It falls while the months lose money, turns up at break-even, and crosses zero at payback.

title: 2 · Plan a new area: the three parts
lines: This is Kelvin in finance. Projects also opens from the Money screen. Tap Projects.
A new area to think about. Tap New project.
Give it a name.
If the area already exists in Zuri, pick it here. Zuri then pulls the real customers and payments for tracking by itself. Kijabe is new, so we leave it.
A note about the area helps the partners remember why.
Create.
Part A: the start-up costs. Everything paid once, before the first customer. This is the money you need to get back.
Four kilometres of fiber…
at two hundred and ninety thousand shillings a kilometre, laid. Zuri multiplies them.
The equipment at the hub.
Labour.
And contingency: extra for surprises. Builds almost always cost more than planned. Ten to fifteen percent is normal.
Routers: Zuri pays one for every new customer, in the month they join, unless it is in the install fee.
Part B: the running costs, every month, with or without customers.
Backhaul: pick a real quote. Bayobab, one hundred megabits, fourteen thousand a month.
Two staff…
at twenty-two thousand each.
Rent for a small shop.
Part C: customers and money in. This is the part to argue about: small changes here move the payback month the most.
How many homes and businesses the fiber passes.
Sign-ups by month one, three, six, twelve and twenty-four.
What does a customer pay? Zuri already knows Zuri A's average from the billing website. Tap Use it.
The install fee.
And how many leave each month, out of every hundred.
Zuri says how many customers you will really have, after the leavers.
And the answer updates as you type. It saves by itself.

title: 3 · Reading the chart, the what-ifs and the table
lines: Back on Narok. Under the answer: the start-up, the running costs, the profit in the first twelve, twenty-four and thirty-six months, and the three-year return.
What if we are wrong? This grid gives the payback month if fewer people join, or more, and if the monthly bill is ten percent lower or higher. The bold one is the plan.
Read the low row first. If it still pays back in a time you can live with, the plan is safe. If it says never, agree now what you would do if sign-ups are slow.
Month by month: customers, money in, costs, profit, and the cash so far. Break-even and payback are marked in green.
Show twelve, twenty-four, thirty-six or sixty months.

title: 4 · A loan, comparing two areas, and sharing
lines: Narok is big, so the plan includes a loan. Open part D.
Five million at sixteen percent over three years. Zuri works out the monthly repayment and the interest, and counts the repayment as a cost.
So the partners see the payback with the loan: less of their own money at the start, but less profit each month while it is repaid.
Two areas? Compare them side by side.
Start-up, payback, the most money tied up, profit and cash after three years, and the payback if take-up is low. The star marks the faster payback.
A smaller area can pay back sooner, even if a bigger one makes more in the end. Look at both.
To share: Copy for WhatsApp gives a short summary with the why, ready for the partners' group.
And the one-page report, for a meeting or as a PDF.
It explains every number in plain words, with the questions the partners should agree on.

title: 5 · We're doing it — asking for the go-ahead
lines: The partners agreed on Narok. Kelvin taps We're doing it.
He picks the launch month: month one, the first month with customers.
Send it for the second OK.
Now it waits. The same rule as money out: a second partner or finance person must approve, never the person who asked. While it waits, the numbers can't change.
In practice you can play the second person. In real life it is Jerry's own phone. The next chapter does that.

title: 5b · The second OK — the plan is locked
lines: This is Jerry. Narok is waiting for his OK. Open it.
He checks the numbers, then taps Approve.
The plan is now locked as the baseline: the yardstick. It never changes. From now on Zuri compares what really happens against it, every month.
The log keeps every step: who asked, who approved, and when.

title: 6 · Things change — update the forecast
lines: Suswa went live five months ago. The approved plan is locked, but what we expect can change: a new quote, slower sign-ups. That is the forecast.
Jerry hears the monthly bill in Suswa is lower than planned. Open part C.
Seventeen hundred, not eighteen hundred.
The answer shows the new payback, and what the locked plan said.
Save the forecast.
Zuri lists exactly what changed.
And asks why. The partners will read it.
Save.
The log: the new forecast, who, when and why, and the earlier change Kelvin made when the fiber quote went up.

title: 7 · Actual against the plan
lines: Every month, Zuri compares Suswa with the plan. First, in plain words: on track, behind or ahead, and by how much cash.
And the payback month now: what really happened so far, plus the forecast for the rest, against what the plan said.
Last month is not confirmed yet. Zuri already filled in what it found on the billing website. Kelvin taps to confirm.
Customers connected at the end of the month: Zuri found eighty-six. He confirms.
Save.
Then the money collected that month.
Save.
Start-up spent against the plan, customers, money in and running costs so far. Green is on plan or better, orange up to fifteen percent worse, red more.
Three lines. Grey dashes: the plan. Green: what really happened. Orange: where it is heading now.
Month by month, actual against the plan, with the difference in shillings and percent.
The build, line by line: fiber cost more than planned, the rest was close.
Where the numbers come from. Zuri pulls expenses tagged to the project, and the payments and billing figures for Zuri D, by itself. Anything else, Kelvin types here.
In Money out, spending in Zuri D is tagged to Suswa by itself. Change it if it is not a project cost.

title: 8 · Projects in the Friday report and on Home
lines: Home shows every project in one line: Suswa's state, and Narok being planned.
And the Friday report has one line per project, so the partners see it every week without asking.
At the start of each month, the Zuri manager puts a task on finance's list: confirm last month's actuals for each live project.

title: 9 · Your turn — plan, go, track
lines: That is Projects. Now try it yourself, in practice. Nothing here is real.
Every chapter is on the Learn page, to watch again any time.

title: 1 · Why receipts matter for Zuri
lines: This series is about receipts: the small paper or message that proves where Zuri money went. First, why it matters. This is Kelvin, in finance, on Friday.
Every Friday, Zuri adds up the week: how much was spent, how many spends have a receipt, and how many are still missing.
One: the tax office, KRA. When Zuri pays tax on its profit, every cost must be proven. A cost with no proper receipt can be refused, and then Zuri pays tax on money it never made.
Two: VAT. Zuri can only claim back the VAT on a receipt that shows the supplier's KRA PIN. No receipt, no claim. On a busy month that is thousands of shillings.
Three: trust. Jerry is far away, and the partners share the profit. A receipt for every shilling means nobody has to wonder, and nobody is blamed by mistake.
Four: the books. Every expense here is checked against the bank and M-Pesa statements. A receipt with the M-Pesa code makes that check automatic.
Expenses with a camera button have the photo saved with them. Tap it, and the receipt opens, from anywhere, for anyone allowed to see that expense.
Here it is: the shop, the PIN, the items, the total. No more lost papers in a drawer.
So the rule is simple: spend Zuri money, get a receipt, snap it the same day. The next videos show exactly how. It takes less than a minute.

title: 2 · Snapping a receipt on a job, step by step
lines: This is Peter, a field technician. He is at a customer's house and had to buy connectors on the way. Let's open the job.
On every job there is this box: spent money on this job? Snap the receipt. Tap it.
The receipt page already knows which job this is for, so the office can see what each job really cost.
Lay the receipt flat, in good light, with the whole paper in the picture. Then tap Take a photo, and press the camera button.
Zuri makes the photo small enough for weak signal. Here, reading with AI is switched on, so Zuri reads the receipt and fills in the boxes.
The photo is kept. Tap it any time to see it bigger.
The boxes Zuri filled are marked yellow. The shop: Kamau Hardware.
The amount. Always look at the paper and check this number. It is the most important box.
What it was for: Zuri suggests it. Equipment, because Peter usually buys equipment at this shop. Tap a suggestion, or choose from the list.
The area is filled from Peter's own area, and the date is today. Change them only if they are wrong.
Paid with: M-Pesa, cash or bank. Zuri remembers what you used last time.
The M-Pesa code from the receipt. With the code, finance can match this spend to the M-Pesa statement automatically.
And the receipt line says Photo saved. Nothing more to choose.
Everything looks right. Tap Save. That's three taps: the button, the camera, and Save.
Zuri goes straight back to the job. The photo uploads by itself in the background.
Under Me, My receipts shows everything Peter recorded, with a photo button on each one. Only Peter and the finance team can see them.

title: 3 · Checking and fixing what was read
lines: Reading is a helper, not the boss. You are the boss. This video shows how to check, and fix, what Zuri read. Peter bought fuel for the motorbike.
He snaps the fuel receipt.
When Zuri is sure, it says: check the yellow boxes. When it is not sure, the message is orange: check every box carefully. Blurry or folded receipts are harder to read.
Look at the paper. The total is one thousand. If Zuri read a different number, tap the box and type the right one.
The shop name. Write it the same way every time, like Rubis Maai Mahiu, so Zuri learns it.
The chips are suggestions. Usually means what this shop was called before. Looks like means words on the receipt, like petrol. The robot chip is the AI's guess.
If none is right, choose from the list. Fuel for work is Transport and Fuel.
Working in Zuri B today? Change the area, so the cost lands on the right area's books.
The date. If you forgot yesterday and snap it today, change the date to the day you paid.
Paid with cash? Tap Cash.
Under More are the VAT, the supplier's KRA PIN and what was bought. Zuri fills them from the receipt. Finance needs the PIN to claim the VAT back.
The PIN starts with a letter, has nine numbers, and ends with a letter. Check it against the paper.
And a short note: what it was for. Fuel for the market jobs.
All checked. Save.
Saved, with the photo. If you find a mistake later, tell finance: they can correct it.

title: 4 · Pasting an M-Pesa message
lines: Many payments have no paper at all: just the M-Pesa message. The message is the receipt. Kelvin paid the hardware shop from the till. Tap Paste M-Pesa message.
In the Messages app, press and hold the M-Pesa message, tap Copy, come back, and paste it here.
Tap Read the message. It works with no signal and costs nothing: Zuri reads it on the phone itself.
Zuri knows the kinds of M-Pesa message: paid to a till, sent to a Paybill with an account number, sent to a person, a cash withdrawal, airtime, and Fuliza.
It filled in the shop, the amount, the date and the code.
And the category, learned from history: payments to this shop were Equipment before. No AI needed for that.
The receipt line says the M-Pesa message is the receipt. Save.
Another one: a Paybill payment for the office electricity.
For a Paybill, the account number goes in the note. If the person was paid by Send money, their phone number goes there too, and the transaction cost.
For finance, Zuri also sees when a payment is one of this month's bills, like KPLC, and can tick it off the bill list at the same time.
One warning. If you paste a message where money came IN, Zuri tells you: that is not a spend.
Money in goes in Money in, or comes from the billing website. Fuliza messages work too: only the Fuliza fee is a cost; the payment itself is in the other message.

title: 5 · Repeats, and matching the statement
lines: Money must be counted once, never twice. Zuri checks every M-Pesa or bank code you type.
Peter forwarded this message: fuel at Total, two thousand. Kelvin pastes it.
Green: already in the M-Pesa statement, matched. This payment came in with the statement import, but nobody had said what it was for. Saving links the two, so it is counted once, with its reason.
Fuel. Save.
Now a message that was already recorded: Brian's hardware receipt from three days ago.
Red: already recorded, with who recorded it and when. Saving again would count it twice, so the Save button stops.
Only if it really is a different payment with the same code, which almost never happens, tap Save anyway. Otherwise, just leave the page.
In Money out, each expense shows its receipt. When statements are imported later, Zuri also links expenses by their code, so the books never count a payment twice.

title: 6 · No signal — what happens
lines: Peter is in the valley, with no signal. For this video we switched the phone to no signal. Watch the badge at the top.
He snaps the receipt anyway.
Zuri says: no signal, type it, the photo will upload later. With no signal, Zuri cannot read the photo, so Peter types the few boxes himself.
The shop.
The amount.
What it was for. The suggestions still work from what this phone remembers.
Save.
The yellow badge: one thing waiting to send. The expense and the photo are kept safely on the phone, even if it is switched off.
In My receipts it shows: not sent yet. Peter can carry on working.
Under Me, Waiting to send lists it. Important: do not sign out while things are waiting.
Now the signal comes back.
It sent by itself: the expense, and then the photo. Nothing to press. If something cannot send, a red badge appears; tap it, then Retry.

title: 7 · The AI setting (partners)
lines: Reading receipts with AI is a setting, and only the partners can change it. This is Jerry, under Me, Admin, Settings.
It starts Off. Off means the photo is still kept with every expense, but people type the details themselves. Free.

On means the photo is sent to Zuri's reading helper, Claude, made by Anthropic. It reads the shop, amount, date, code, VAT and PIN, and suggests the category from Zuri's own list. It writes nothing by itself: the person checks and taps Save.
The cost: about three to five shillings per receipt, from Jerry's Anthropic account. A hundred receipts a month is about four hundred shillings. Each person can read up to forty a day.
Zuri shows who changed it, and when.
With it On, a snapped receipt is read in a few seconds.
Like this. If the reading fails, or there is no signal, nobody sees an error: Zuri just asks them to type it, and the photo is kept.
To stop the cost at any time, tap Off. Everything keeps working; people type instead.
Now with it Off, the same photo…
Zuri says: type the details, reading is switched off. The partners decide. Jerry can switch it on when the boys are ready.

title: 8 · Missing receipts: the nudge and the task
lines: Sometimes there is no receipt at the time. Peter saved an expense with No receipt yet, chase it. Two days later, the Zuri manager put this on his list by itself.
It is also in his morning WhatsApp nudge, so he sees it before he leaves home. No AI is needed for this: it is a simple rule that runs every morning.
My receipts shows which one: the hardware shop, three thousand eight hundred and fifty. Peter goes back and asks the shop for the receipt.
Then he taps Snap it now.
And takes the photo. That is all.
The receipt is attached, and the expense now says photo.
The next morning the manager sees the receipt is there and closes the task by itself. Nobody has to chase him.

title: 8b · Chasing receipts (finance)
lines: Finance gets a second kind of task. Money left the M-Pesa or bank statement, and after three days there is still no expense with that code.
The task says how much, to whom, and on which day. Kelvin finds out what it was, then records it with the code, so the two link and the task closes by itself.
His own missing receipts come here too, just like Peter's.
Every morning, the WhatsApp nudges include each person's missing receipts. Open WhatsApp, press send, mark it sent.
Cash today also counts the expenses still missing a receipt this month, per area.
And Money out shows every expense's receipt at a glance: photo, M-Pesa message, paper filed, or no receipt.

title: 9 · Reading “Receipts this week” on Friday
lines: Friday. The report for the partners now has a Receipts this week part. It covers the last seven days.
Spent: the total, and how many payments. With a receipt: photo, M-Pesa message, or paper filed. Missing: how many, and how much money that is.
By category: where the money went. Fuel jumping, or equipment much higher than usual, is a question to ask.
The five biggest spends, with who recorded them. Tap the camera to see any receipt.
Partners can look at the receipt right here.
And the missing list, with who recorded each one and the amount. Chase these before Monday.
The same part is in the report text. Copy for WhatsApp, and paste it in the partners' group. The Zuri manager's own Friday report includes it too.
The month export to Excel now has a Receipt photo column, for the accountant.

title: 10 · Your turn — try it all yourself
lines: That is receipts in Zuri. Now try it yourself, in practice. Nothing here is real.
Take a photo of any paper, a shop receipt or even a page, and save it as a receipt.
Copy an old M-Pesa message from your own phone and paste it here. Zuri reads it on your phone; nothing is sent.
Your receipts are under Me. To try the finance and partner parts, use Me, Try another job.

title: Doing a job, start to finish
lines: These are your jobs. Today's jobs are at the top. A red dot means urgent. Do those first.
Looking for one job? Type a name, a phone number or the job number here.
Tap a job to open it.
Here is the customer. Tap Call to phone them before you go.
Open map shows the way to the house. If there is no pin yet, you will drop one when you get there.
When you arrive, tap I'm starting now. The office can see you are on site.
When the work is done, tap what you found. You can tap more than one, or type your own words.
Then tap what you did.
Did the customer pay you? Tap No, Cash, or M-Pesa.
Type how much. For M-Pesa, type the code from the customer's message, so the office can match the payment.
Last, tap Job finished. Even with no signal it is saved, and it sends later.
The job leaves your list. On to the next one. Well done!

title: Photos, parts, map pins, new jobs
lines: Let's open a job.
Take a photo of the problem, and of your finished work. Tap Add photo. It works with no signal too: it uploads later.
Write every part you use: routers, cable, connectors. Put the serial number for routers. This is how we keep track of stock.

Standing at the customer's house? Tap Drop pin here. If the house already has a pin, it says Move pin to here. Do it outside. If the phone says the location is not accurate, wait a minute and try again. A good pin saves the next tech an hour. Drop it before you tap Job finished: once the job is done the button goes away.
Found a new problem while you are out? Tap Log a job.
Write what is wrong, in a few words.
Tap Save job. It goes on your list, and the office sees it.

title: Payment follow-up calls
lines: Every morning Zuri opens a Payment follow-up job for each customer whose internet ran out. These are your calls for the day.
Open one.
You can see when their package ran out, and how much it costs. Tap Call.
After the call, tap what happened. No answer: it comes back tomorrow. Says paid: we check the next billing import. Wants to stop: the job closes.
If they promise to pay, tap Will pay, and choose the day.
In three days, for example.
Every call is written here, so anyone can see the whole story of this customer.

Billnasi already texted them three days before and switched them off. Our part starts after the cutoff. The steps on top show where this customer is: day one, help them reconnect. Day three, is anything wrong? Day seven, we miss you. Day fourteen, a last check-in. Day thirty, a kind goodbye.
The message for today's step is written for you. Tap Text it, or WhatsApp it, and press send. The job then comes back on the day of the next step.
If they say the internet was not working, tap Service problem. A fault job opens for them, so a technician goes.
When the customer pays, the job closes by itself. You never need to close it.

title: A customer calls with a problem
lines: A customer calls: no internet. Start a new job. Type their name or phone number.
Tap the right customer.
Choose the type of job. Fault means no internet or slow internet.
Write what the customer says, in their words.
Send it to a tech, and choose the visit day. Not sure who? Leave it, and the office decides.
Tap Save job.
Now tap to tell the tech on WhatsApp. The message has the customer, the problem and the map. Just press send.

title: Finding a customer
lines: Customers holds everyone Zuri serves. Search by name, phone or account number.
Tap a customer to open them.
Here is everything about them: package, phone, where they live, and when their payment runs out.
Below are their payments, and every job we have done for them.
To open a job for this customer, tap New job. Their details are filled in for you.

title: Daily money: count, record, check
lines: Money starts with Cash today: what is in the bank, the M-Pesa float, bills still owing, and cash left after bills.
Red and orange boxes tell you what to do, like a float that is too low, or a bill that is due.
Count the cash at least once a week, and every Friday. Look at the bank app and the M-Pesa account, and type what each one says.
Tap Save cash count. The forecast for the next 30 days starts from this number.
Paid something by M-Pesa? Copy the confirmation message and paste it here.
Tap Read the message. Zuri fills in the code, the amount, who was paid, the date, and the new balance.
It even sees this is the KPLC bill, and ticks it off the bill list for you.
Check the boxes, then tap Save expense.
Money that comes in, like hotspot sales or installation fees, goes in Money in. Customers' monthly payments come from the billing website, so you don't type those.

title: Paying the monthly bills
lines: Every monthly bill is here: the due day, how much is paid, and how much is still owing.
When you send the money, tap Pay.
Choose where the money came from: M-Pesa, bank or cash. Part payments are fine.
Type the M-Pesa or bank code.

Tap Pay and record it. It is recorded in Money out automatically, so you never type it twice. Then a second person, a partner or another finance person, approves it, and only then does the bill count it as paid.
At the start of a new month, tap Copy last month's bills. Then change any amount that is different.

title: Bank & M-Pesa statements
lines: Every account Zuri money passes through is listed here: the bank, the business M-Pesa, and any phone customers pay into.
Once a month, bring in each statement. Excel, CSV or the M-Pesa PDF all work. Bringing the same one twice is safe: repeats are skipped.
Then sort the transactions. Choose what each one is: a customer payment, a bill, or money moving between our own accounts.
Tap Always sort like this, or tick always before you choose, to teach Zuri. Next time, every transaction like this one is sorted by itself.
Many the same? Tick them, choose once, and tap Sort ticked.
Profit by month adds it all up: income, expenses and profit, month by month. The more you sort, the truer it is.

title: Running the company from Home
lines: Home is the whole company on one page. The Zuri manager card tells you what it noticed this morning.
Needs attention lists the most important problems first. Tap one to go straight to it.
Customers: how many are active, how many have paid, and how much is late.
This chart is our cash for the next 30 days: renewals coming in, bills going out. If it goes below zero, Zuri warns you weeks before.
Who paid shows every customer this month: paid, late, or not due yet. Call or WhatsApp late payers from here.
On Friday, the report writes itself. Tap Copy, and paste it into the partners' WhatsApp group.
Every morning the manager writes a short WhatsApp for each staff member. Tap Open WhatsApp, press send, and mark it sent.
The Manager log shows everything the manager did. It only writes tasks, notes and reports. It never touches money or customers.

title: Adding a new staff member
lines: New staff make their own account on the sign-in page, with their phone number. Then they wait here, switched off.
Choose their job. A field tech sees only their own jobs. Call center sees jobs and customers. Office finance sees money too.
Choose their area.
Switch them on, and tap Save. They can now sign in.
Who sees what lets you hide private details, like a customer's ID number, from some jobs.

title: Headquarters: the whole company, and a message to anyone
lines: Partners have one more screen: Headquarters. It is at the top of Home. Tap it.
Headquarters is the whole company on one screen. First, Needs a decision: payments waiting for an OK, and urgent tasks. Tap one to go there.
Areas side by side: customers, how many paid, late payers, open faults, installs waiting, overdue visits and cash. Tap an area to open its Home.
Live activity: what everyone did, newest first. New jobs, finished jobs, payments, and money waiting for an OK.
Choose one area, and how far back to look: six hours, up to seven days.
The team, by area, and when each person last did something in Zuri. Quiet all day? Call them, or tap the envelope to message them.
To message many people at once, tap Message.
Pick who gets it: everyone, one area, one job like Field tech, or tick people one by one.
Write it once. Each person gets their own copy, with their own name.
Tap Next: send.
Now tap WhatsApp or SMS for each person, and press send there. Zuri never sends anything by itself. Headquarters only reads: it never changes the company's records.

title: 1 · Home
lines: Chapter one: Home. At the top: who you are, and the area picker. All areas shows the whole company; pick one area, like Zuri A, to see that area only. Every screen follows this choice.
Partners also get Headquarters: every area side by side, live activity, and a message to anyone. It has its own video.
The Zuri manager card: when it last ran, how many things are on your list, and its warnings for today.
Needs attention: the most important problems, most urgent first. Each one is a link to the screen where you fix it.
Customers: active customers, how many are paid up, how many have run out, the monthly recurring revenue if everyone pays, renewals due in the next seven days, and customers with no map pin.
Packages: how many customers are on each package, and the money each package brings in per month.
Service: open faults and how many were fixed this month, installs waiting, visits today and this week, overdue visits, and payment follow-ups.
Under it, the next service jobs, with the day and the technician. Tap one to open it.
Money, for finance and partners only: cash now from the last count, the lowest point in the next thirty days, cash in thirty days, bills still owing, and last month's profit from the statements.
The chart: the cash balance day by day for the next month. Green bars are renewals coming in, red bars are bills going out.
Sales from the billing website, month by month: subscriptions against hotspot.
And income against expenses from the sorted statements. Tap refresh at the top right to reload all of it.

title: 2 · Tasks
lines: Chapter two: Tasks. My day, Team, Add a task, and, for finance and the partners, WhatsApp nudges and the Manager log.
Partners also get Run the manager now, which runs the morning rules on the spot.
A task: the tick box, the title, who it is for, where it came from, when it is due, and a lock if only finance can see it.
Open, if the task points at a page or a customer, and Notes to talk about it.
Team: everyone's open tasks, grouped by person. Filter by a group or a person here.
Show done brings back the last seven days of finished tasks.
Add a task. What needs doing: a few plain words.
Details: anything that helps them do it. Optional.
Who should do it: yourself, a person, or a whole group, like Field techs or Finance.
Due: the day. Leave it blank for whenever.
Priority: normal, high, urgent or low. High and urgent go to the top of their list.
Money task: tick this and only finance and the partners can see it.
WhatsApp nudges: the morning message for each person who has a phone number on their account. Open WhatsApp, send it, Mark sent.
The Manager log: every run, what it created, closed and escalated, and its warnings.

title: 3 · Jobs and a new job
lines: Chapter three: Jobs. To do, Done, or All.
Search by the customer's name, their phone, or the job number. It filters as you type.
All techs, or one technician's jobs.
A job row: a red dot if urgent, the customer, the job number, the kind of job and the problem, the area and landmark, the technician, the visit day, and the status.
Payment follow-ups open by themselves each morning. Check now runs that check straight away.
New job. Customer: type a name, phone or account number and tap the right one. Leave it empty for a new-install enquiry.
Area, and the type of job: fault, new install, payment follow-up, move connection, disconnect, site survey, or other.
What is wrong or needed, in the customer's words.
Caller name and phone, if the person calling is not the customer.
Priority: normal, urgent or low.
Send to tech: choose the technician, or leave it for later. And the visit day.
Save job puts it on the technician's list straight away.

title: 4 · Inside a job
lines: Chapter four: inside a job. Let's open a fault.
The job number, the kind, and the status: waiting for a tech, assigned, in progress, done, or cancelled.
The problem, as the customer described it.
The customer card: name, area, account, package and rate, when their payment runs out, the landmark, and Call buttons for each phone number.
Open map and Send pin, if there is a pin. Drop pin here, or Move pin to here, saves where the technician is standing.
Who's going, and when: the technician, the visit day, and the priority. Save, Cancel job, or Reopen.
The work. What did you find: tap the round buttons, or type.
What did you do: the same.
Did the customer pay you: No, Cash, or M-Pesa. Then how much, and for M-Pesa, the code from the customer's message.
Job finished closes it. I'm starting now marks it in progress. Save for later keeps what you typed.
Parts and equipment: the item, its serial number if it has one, and how many. Remove takes one off.
Photos: add a picture of the problem and the finished work.
Notes: everything that happened on this job, by whom and when. Add a note at the bottom.
A payment follow-up has one more card.
After the call: No answer, Will pay with a day, Says paid, or Wants to stop.

Below it, the path after the cutoff. Billnasi texts customers before their package runs out; we follow up after: day one reconnect help, day three is anything wrong, day seven we miss you, day fourteen last check-in, day thirty a kind goodbye. Today's message is written for you: Text it or WhatsApp it, and the job comes back on the next step's day. Service problem opens a fault job.

title: 5 · Customers
lines: Chapter five: Customers. Search by name, phone or account number.
Filter by status: active, lead, suspended, disconnected, or any.
A customer row: name, phone, account, package, area, landmark, and a warning if there is no map pin. Fifty per page.

Map shows every customer with a pin, green if paid up, red if they ran out, for the area chosen at the top, plus the office, cabinets and towers as square icons. Tap a customer to see how far its nearest hub is. New customer adds one by hand; most come in from the billing website.
Open one.
The customer: name and status, area and landmark.
Call, Map, Send pin, Drop pin here, New job for this customer, and Edit.
Their details: phone numbers, email, account number, billing website ID, ID number, package and rate, paid until, install date, and any custom fields. Field techs see only what the admin allows.
Payments: every payment we know of, with the date, amount, how, and the M-Pesa code.
Jobs: every job ever done for them.
Edit opens every field.
Full name. Area. Status.
Phone, second phone, email.
Account number, billing website ID, national ID.
Package, monthly rate in shillings, install date.
Directions or landmark: how a technician finds the house. Notes for anything else.
Custom fields the admin added, like the router model. Save customer at the bottom.

title: 5b · The map
lines: Chapter five b: the map. Every customer who has a pin, for the area chosen at the top. Pick one area at the top to see only that area.
The colours: green means paid up, red means their package ran out, grey means not active. The numbers are counted for you.
Hubs: the office, the OLT room, cabinets, towers and the store, drawn as square icons. Untick this to hide them.
Pinch or use plus and minus to zoom. Drag to move around Maai Mahiu.
Tap any pin. It shows the customer, their package and rate, the landmark, and how far the nearest hub is — so you know which cabinet serves that house.
Pins come from the technician tapping Drop pin here while standing at the house. This line tells you how many active customers still have no pin. Every job is a chance to add one.

title: 5c · A new customer
lines: Chapter five c: adding a new customer. From Customers, tap New customer. It is the same form as Edit, starting empty.
Full name first: the name on the account.
The area, like Zuri A. This decides whose map and lists they appear on.
Status: lead if they have only asked, active once they are installed and paying.
Phone numbers: the M-Pesa number first, so payments can be matched to them.
Account number and billing website ID: the same as in Billnasi, so the two never disagree. Zuri warns you if one is already used.
Directions or landmark: how a technician finds the house without calling. Be generous: "blue gate after the church".
Save customer. The GPS pin comes later, when the technician stands at the house and taps Drop pin here.

title: 6 · Money: Cash today
lines: Chapter six: Money. Six sections: Today, Record, Bills, Customers, Statements, Report. Some have a second row of pages.
Cash today. First: customer payments this month, other cash in like hotspot, and expenses logged.
Then each area: the bank balance from the last count, the M-Pesa float against its target, bills still owing, and cash after bills: bank plus M-Pesa minus what is owed.
The alerts: float below target, cash after bills negative, bills due, Friday count due, missing receipts.
And three shortcuts: Cash count, Log expense, Cash ahead.

title: 7 · Count the cash
lines: Chapter seven: Count the cash. The area and the date.
Bank balance, from the bank app. M-Pesa balance, from the business account. Leave one empty and it keeps the figure from the last count.
Counted by, and a note for Jerry if something needs saying.
Recent counts below. The × removes a wrong one.

title: 8 · Money out
lines: Chapter eight: Money out. Paste the M-Pesa confirmation message here and tap Read the message: it fills the code, amount, payee, date and the new balance.
Area and date.
Paid to: start typing and known payees appear. Category: what kind of cost.
Amount in shillings. Paid from: M-Pesa, bank or cash. The M-Pesa or bank code.
Receipt: digital, paper and filed, or none, chase it. No receipt stays on the list until it is found.
More details: who approved it, VAT on the receipt, the supplier's KRA PIN for VAT, and a note. If the payee matches a bill, a tick box offers to count it against that bill.
Save expense. This month's expenses are listed below, with a receipt pill.

title: 9 · Money in
lines: Chapter nine: Money in, for money that is not a customer's monthly payment: hotspot, installation fee, reconnection fee, equipment sale, other.
Amount, and where it was received: M-Pesa, bank or cash.
From whom, the M-Pesa code, and a note. Save cash in.

title: 10 · Bills
lines: Chapter ten: Bills. The arrows move between months.
Each bill: name and category, the due day, the amount, what is paid, what is owing. Pay opens the pay sheet; the pencil changes the amount or removes the bill.
Copy last month's bills makes the new month in one tap.
Add a bill: area, the name, the amount, the due day of the month, the category, and Pay to: the paybill and account, or the phone number the money goes to.

title: 10b · Pay run
lines: The Pay run: what to pay today. Build today's list collects the bills that are due and the staff whose pay day has come.
To pay now, coming in three days, and sent this month.
Each line: a bill or a person, the amount, and the number to pay. Copy number, then send it in the M-Pesa app.
Back in Zuri, tap Sent, type the M-Pesa code, and it is recorded as an expense. Skip puts it off for now.

Staff and pay, next to the Pay run under Bills: everyone Zuri pays, with their M-Pesa number, salary and pay day. Only finance and the partners see it. Casual staff paid by the day or the job are paid by hand in Money out.

title: 11 · Who paid
lines: Chapter eleven: Who paid. Collected against expected, how many paid in full, late or part-paid and what they still owe, and not due yet.
Late, Part paid, No history, Not due yet, Paid, All.
Each customer: rate, what they paid this month, when they ran out or renew, how reliably they pay. Call and WhatsApp buttons for the late ones.

title: 12 · Next 30 days
lines: Chapter twelve: the next thirty days. The lowest point and when, the month-end balance, expected money in, bills still to pay, and the upside if late payers pay.
The chart: the balance day by day.
Start from today's balance: type it if there is no fresh count. Update redraws.
One-off money in or out: a day, an amount with a minus for money out, and what it is. Funding from Jerry, a generator repair.
Day by day: customers, other in, bills out, one-offs, balance, and a note of which bills land that day.

title: 13 · Bank & M-Pesa statements
lines: Chapter thirteen: Statements. Every account money passes through: name, kind, area, owner, how far the statement goes, the balance, and how many lines still to sort.
Import: which account, and the file: Excel, CSV, or the M-Pesa PDF. Repeats are skipped.
Add an account: name, kind, which area if any, and whose it is.

title: 14 · Sort them
lines: Chapter fourteen: Sort them. All accounts or one; to sort, or already sorted.
Tick several, pick one category, Sort ticked.
Each line: the description, date, account, code, and the amount. Choose the category.
Always: tick it before you choose, and Zuri sorts every line like this by itself next time. Chose first? The line then offers Always sort like this.

title: 15 · Profit by month
lines: Chapter fifteen: Profit by month. Income, expenses and profit for the latest month.
Where the money went, by category.
The table: every income and expense category, month by month, with totals and profit. Transfers between our own accounts and owner money are left out.

title: 16 · Friday report and bringing in files
lines: Chapter sixteen: the Friday report writes itself from this week's numbers.
Copy for WhatsApp, and Export to CSV for a spreadsheet of the whole month.
Bring in a file: a customer list or customer payments, from Billnasi or the second billing website.
Area if the file does not say, then the file. Zuri reads the headings and asks you to check them.

title: 17 · Admin
lines: Chapter seventeen: Admin. People: everyone who signed up. Their job: field tech, call center, office staff with a finance or technical department, or admin. Their area. On or off. Save.
Who sees what: for each customer field, which jobs may see it. Untick ID numbers for field techs, for example.
Custom fields: add your own customer field. A name, a kind: text, number, date, yes or no, or pick from a list, and the choices.
Areas: each area's M-Pesa float target, and whether it is in use. Zuri C is already here: tick In use when it opens. A brand-new area is added here.
Price list: the packages Zuri sells, and the monthly price of each. On a customer, Zuri offers these and fills in the rate. To change a price, save the same name again.
Company and hubs. The company card: the name, phones, the M-Pesa Paybill and the KRA PIN. The reminder texts to customers use the name and the Paybill from here.
Hubs: the office, the OLT room, splitter cabinets, towers and the store. They show on the customer map for everyone.
To add one, stand at the place and tap Where I'm standing, or tap the map. Give it a name and an area, and save.

title: 17b · Access codes
lines: Chapter seventeen b: access codes, for partners. A code lets a phone into practice, the Testers' List and the training copy. The real app keeps its own logins.
Make a code: Zuri suggests one. You can type your own instead.
Label: who it is for, like October testers, so you remember later.
Kind: Tester, Demo or trial, or Staff.
How many days it works, and how many phones may use it. Then Make the code.

Every code is listed with who used it and when they were last seen. Copy sends a ready message with the code already inside the link — nobody has to type it. Plus thirty days extends it. Revoke switches it off; those phones stop the next time they open Zuri.

title: 18 · Me
lines: Chapter eighteen: Me. Your job and area, and whether you are online.
Waiting to send: work saved on this phone that has not reached the server yet. Send now, Retry, or Discard.
More: Snap a receipt, My receipts, Learn Zuri, Testing Zuri, Admin, and Bring in a file.
Screen: like my phone, light, or dark.
Sign out, and the version line. That is every screen and every field. Thank you for watching.

title: 1 · Why we don't just switch it on
lines: This is Dickson. Zuri is nearly ready, and the team is keen to start. So why not just switch it on next Monday? This card on Home is the answer. It is called Getting ready.
First, the good news. The team can start learning today. Practice uses pretend customers, so nobody can break anything. Training the techs does not have to wait.
But using Zuri for real is different. Zuri is only as true as what we put in it. If the customer list is wrong on day one, the techs stop trusting it by day three. And trust is hard to win back.
So before the real start, a few things must be true. Tap the card.
Fifty-seven steps. That sounds like a lot. But most take under an hour, and you only ever look at one at a time.
Aim for about ten weeks. In a busy business, maybe twelve or fourteen. That is OK. The order matters more than the speed.
This is my next step. Just one. When I tick it, the next one appears.

title: 2 · The whole list, in ten parts
lines: Here is the whole list, once, so you can see its shape. Then you can forget it and go one step at a time.
Part one: agree the plan. One sit-down together, a weekly check-in, a kind message to the team, and a start month with room to spare. These are done already.
Part two: one home for files and passwords. Google Drive or Microsoft 365, one, not both, owned by the company, not by one person.
Part three: WhatsApp. A company number, the right team groups with pinned rules, and broadcast lists for customers. Not groups. In a group every customer sees every other customer's number.

Part four: write down what is true. Areas, every OLT, cabinet and tower with its GPS, the packages in both billing websites, the staff, and the monthly bills. If you are not sure, write check. A blank is better than a wrong number.
Part five: the money starting point. One start date, and on that day: the bank, M-Pesa, the cash in each area, what we owe and what is owed to us.

Part six: the customers. Export from Billnasi and from the second billing website, clean out repeats and test accounts, fix the phone numbers, and then phone twenty customers to prove the list is true.
Part seven is the big one. The live Zuri starts fresh and empty. Jerry builds it, and you fill it only with the lists you checked. Nothing from testing comes across.
Part eight: training. Partners first, then the techs and the office, then one practice day all together. This part can start any time.
Part nine: go live, gently. Both partners say yes. One area first. The old way and Zuri side by side for a week. Then one more area each week.
And part ten, after we are running: map pins, customer emails, paid messages if we need them, and a monthly look after the system. No rush.

title: 3 · One step at a time
lines: This is Kelvin. The list opens on one step: mine. I can also look at Dickson's, or everyone's.
My next step: make one company account. Only this one. The rest can wait.
Every step says why it matters,
how to do it, in a few short lines,
and when it counts as done. No guessing.
Below it, only the next two. There is no need to look further.
Finished? Tap Done.
I can add a note: a date, a number, a name. Dickson sees it too.
Save.
And the next step appears by itself: make the folders.
Not today? Tap Later. It goes to the back of my line. Nothing is lost.
So the next one comes up instead.
And if something is in the way, tap I am stuck, and write one line.
For example: the bank login is on the old phone.
Ask for help.
It shows here, under waiting for help, and on Jerry's HQ screen. Being stuck is not failing. It tells Jerry where to help. Meanwhile, I carry on with my next step.
One more button: put it in Tasks. The step becomes a normal task, due in a week, so it shows in My day with everything else.

title: 4 · Who does what, and the weekly check-in
lines: This is Jerry. On HQ, the Getting ready card shows how far along we are, each partner's next step, and anything stuck.
Dickson is stuck on the company phone. That is my cue to help, not to push.
I can open anyone's list. Dickson's.
Here is his stuck step. Open it.
Every step has its own page, with the note about what is in the way.
If a step suits someone else better, change who does it, right here. Nobody has to carry a step that is not theirs.
The whole list starts with seven short rules. The most important: meet for thirty minutes once a week, same day, same time, and look at this list together.
And the whole list prints on paper, with tick boxes, for the office wall.
One step at a time, a little each week, and Zuri starts on a true foundation. Be patient with each other. You will get there.
